tone_statements.quote: A linguistic characterization. Kim may have once been a tone language but tone has only limited lexical and grammatical functions in the language as it now exists. Accent now seems to be the crucial prosodic distinction.
tone_statements.locator: section headed 'A linguistic characterization.' (paragraph following the language-vitality assessment), Kim page of the DKB site
tone_statements.summary: Residual/marginal tone: limited lexical and grammatical tone functions surviving in a moribund language, with accent described as the main prosodic contrast (consistent with the known Childs 2020 abstract 'tone is only marginally distinct lexically' and Childs 2025: 41 'tone is less prominent . Bom-Kim').

sources.citation: Childs, G. Tucker. 2025. A grammar of Sherbro. Berlin: Language Science Press (LangSci 403), 582 pp. CC BY. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.15045985
sources.note: Describes Sherbro (sher1258), not Bom-Kim. Ch. 2 Phonology has 2.2 Tone (p. 41-43) and 2.3 Syllable structure but no word-stress section; the only 'stress' mentions are about Pichl's 1967 Sherbro dictionary notation ('5 levels of tone along with 5 levels of stress', p. 190). On Bom-Kim it says only: 'Both lexical and grammatical tone are found in other Bolom-Kisi languages that are still vital (Mani and Kisi), though tone is less prominent in the most moribund Bolom language Bom-Kim' (p. 41, p. 67). sources.quote: A linguistic characterization. Kim may have once been a tone language but tone has only limited lexical and grammatical functions in the language as it now exists. Accent now seems to be the crucial prosodic distinction.

sources.note: States that Kim was probably once a tone language but that tone now has only limited lexical and grammatical functions, and that accent (not tone) now seems to be the crucial prosodic distinction; earlier on the same page Kim's 'status as a tone language' is named as one of its points of linguistic interest. No tone inventory, no examples, nothing on Bom (the Bom page says virtually nothing was known about Bom in 2009).

sources.note: WALDS data sheets follow a fixed template with a short phonology paragraph (consonants, vowels, usually a tone note) plus grammar notes and a wordlist, so a one-line tone statement for Krim is possible; however the PHOIBLE inventory GM 1307 built from this sheet lists 38 segments and no tonemes, so the sheet may give no tone inventory.
